requirements: Reproduce the core contributions of AgentKernelArena: a benchmark of 196 GPU kernel optimization tasks across HIP-to-HIP, Triton-to-Triton, and PyTorch-to-HIP categories, evaluated on production AI coding agents with a gated compile/correctness/performance pipeline and an unseen-configuration generalization protocol.

sub_tasks.requirements: The hardware, driver, and software stack required to run AgentKernelArena is installed and configured correctly.
The GPU hardware and low-level driver stack match the paper's target platform.
Code has been implemented to run all experiments on AMD Instinct MI300X GPU hardware (CDNA3, architecture token gfx942), as specified in Section 4.

verification.spec: Inspect the framework configuration (e.g., src/prompts/cheatsheet/default_cheatsheet.yaml and global config.yaml) and confirm that MI300X is a registered target_gpu_model mapping to architecture token gfx942 (CDNA3). sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that, before the agent runs, compiles the original (unmodified) kernel and profiles its performance using the same commands that will later be used to evaluate the agent's output, storing baseline timings for speedup computation.

Also verify default timeout=3600 is documented in the global config.

sub_tasks.requirements: After the agent session ends, the centralized evaluator runs the compile/correctness/performance commands independently of the agent (i.e., using the same commands as the baseline stage) and does not rely on the agent's self-reported results.

Verify the evaluator ignores the agent-written file, independently invokes the compile/correctness/performance commands, and produces the true (failed correctness) result.

sub_tasks.requirements: The three-phase gated evaluation (compile → correctness → performance) is implemented with strict gating so that later stages run only if earlier stages pass.

Code has been implemented that executes the task's compile_command (e.g., hipcc for HIP, AST validation and import for Triton) and records a compile pass/fail status; failures halt the pipeline for that task and prevent later stages from running.

verification.spec: Run the pipeline on (a) a task whose kernel compiles cleanly and (b) a task whose kernel has been intentionally broken with a syntax error. Confirm that: for (a) the compile stage records success and the pipeline proceeds to correctness; for (b) compile stage records failure and neither correctness nor performance is executed (no correctness/performance artifacts produced). Confirm hipcc is the invoked tool for HIP tasks and that Triton tasks use AST validation + import as the compile check.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that runs the task's correctness_command against the reference implementation (PyTorch module output for HIP-to-HIP and PyTorch-to-HIP; explicit reference functions for Triton-to-Triton) with task-specific tolerances, and gates it so that it executes only if compilation succeeded.

verification.spec: Run the pipeline on (i) a task with a correct kernel and (ii) a task with a kernel that returns intentionally wrong output. Confirm correctness stage runs only if compilation succeeded, compares against the appropriate reference (PyTorch module for HIP-to-HIP/PyTorch-to-HIP, explicit reference function for Triton-to-Triton), applies the task-specific atol/rtol tolerances, and records pass for (i) and fail for (ii). Also confirm that skipping compilation (forced failure) prevents correctness from running.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that runs the task's performance_command only if correctness passed, using 10 warmup and 100 timed iterations with torch.cuda.Event-based GPU timing.

verification.spec: Instrument the performance runner (or inspect its source) and run it on a small task. Confirm exactly 10 warmup iterations and 100 timed iterations are executed, and that timing uses torch.cuda.Event start/end record + synchronize + elapsed_time. Confirm that when correctness is forced to fail, the performance stage does not execute.

sub_tasks.requirements: When compilation fails, the pipeline records the failure and does not attempt correctness or performance; when correctness fails, the pipeline records the failure and does not attempt performance profiling.

Inspect the task_result.yaml (or equivalent report): for the compile failure case, correctness_status and performance_status must be 'not_run'/absent; for the correctness failure case, compile_status='pass', correctness_status='fail', performance_status='not_run'/absent. Verify no performance measurement artifacts exist for either.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that computes per-task speedup as s = t_baseline / t_optimized, and for multi-shape tasks aggregates per-test-case speedups by arithmetic mean.

Confirm the reported s_k equals the arithmetic mean of per-shape ratios (not geometric mean or min). Then patch the optimized runner to return artificial timings (e.g. per-shape ratios [1, 2, 3, 4]) and confirm s_k = 2.5.

verification.spec: Run the pipeline on a task and verify that a task_result.yaml (or equivalent) is written by the evaluator (not the agent) containing at minimum: compile status (bool), correctness status (bool), per-test-case timings (list), and computed speedup (float).

Run the pipeline and verify (via logs or command tracing) that the evaluator invokes exactly those commands, and that they match the commands invoked during the baseline stage.

verification.spec: Run correctness on (a) a HIP-to-HIP task and verify comparison uses PyTorch module output as reference, (b) a Triton-to-Triton task and verify an explicit reference function is used, and (c) a PyTorch-to-HIP task with PyTorch module reference. sub_tasks.requirements: The aggregate metrics (compilation rate, correctness rate, mean speedup, mean score, geometric mean, fast_p, run-to-run sigma_r) are implemented per the definitions in Section 3.3.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that computes the geometric mean of per-task speedup ratios over correct tasks only (speedup > 0), excluding compilation/correctness failures.

verification.spec: Feed the geometric-mean aggregator a list of per-task speedups containing zeros (failed tasks) and positive values. Verify that (a) zero-speedup tasks are excluded, (b) the result equals exp(mean(log(s_i))) over the positive subset, within 1e-6.

verification.spec: Provide a synthetic per-task speedup list containing values both above and below 1x and 2x thresholds. Verify the fast_p function returns the fraction >= p for p=1 and p=2 matching hand-computed expectations, and that the reported output includes both fast_1 and fast_2 columns.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that computes run-to-run sigma_r as the standard deviation over the 3 runs' aggregate mean speedups (and, analogously, over geometric means), reported alongside each aggregate.

verification.spec: Create 3 mock runs with known aggregate mean speedups (e.g., [2.0, 2.5, 3.0]). Do the same for geometric mean aggregates.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that averages each task's metrics across the 3 per-configuration runs before computing aggregate statistics (per-task-averaged aggregation), rather than aggregating raw per-run values.

verification.spec: Build a synthetic dataset with 3 runs x N tasks of per-task speedup values. Verify that the aggregation pipeline first averages each task's metrics across the 3 runs, then computes aggregates over the N per-task averages, rather than pooling all 3N raw values (compare outputs against both computation orders on a case where they differ).

verification.spec: Provide a synthetic list of per-task run-averaged speedups. Verify the reporter emits std, P25, P75, and P90 fields whose values match numpy.std/percentile computed independently to within 1e-6.
